name: Minimum quench energy of HL-LHC RRP Nb3Sn wires with high-heat-capacity tape at 4.2 K and 15 T
plain_name: Measure the smallest heat pulse that makes an accelerator-magnet wire stop superconducting at 15 T
description: Strand test for Nb3Sn accelerator-magnet conductor: a reacted wire on a Ti-6Al-4V barrel is cooled in boiling helium at 4.2 K in transverse field, its Ic is measured with a voltage-tap pair, then at a fixed fraction of Ic heat pulses from strain-gauge heaters are increased until the wire quenches (MQE).
keywords: Measure the smallest heat pulse that makes an accelerator-magnet wire stop superconducting at 15 T

sources.citation: Minimum Quench Energy of Nb3Sn Wires with High Specific Heat Tape (Barzi et al., FERMILAB-PUB-22-133-TD, arXiv:2204.05378)

reported_equipment: FNAL strand test facility (boiling He, transverse field)

requirements.rationale: Ic and MQE are measured at 4.2 K.
The wire is cooled by a boiling helium bath, which sets the heat removal relevant to MQE.
MQE results are reported at 15 T (and 14 T).
Transport current, voltage taps and heater leads must reach the sample.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
